title: POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION OF THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE BY RNA-BINDING PROTEINS
abstract: While transcriptional control of innate immune gene expression is well characterized, almost nothing is known about how pre-mRNA splicing decisions influence, or are influenced by, macrophage activation. I believe each step of RNA processing is just as important, if not more important than the initial transcription of an immune response gene, and RNA-processing can act as a major regulatory node of the innate immune response. title: Identifikacija in analiza dinamičnih zvezdišč RNA v zgodnjem mišjem embrionalnem razvoju
journal: Repository of the University of Ljubljana (University of Ljubljana)
abstract: Early mouse embryonic development proceeds through tightly regulated transitions by specific molecular mechanisms and signalling pathways. Among the implicated mechanisms, complex RNA-protein networks are emerging as important factors. While ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) are known to play a crucial role in the formation of RNP granules and biomolecular condensates, it is still unknown how and which RNA features might contribute to their formation.
